title: Geometric strict henselization over a prime localization
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ a geometric point with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point]. Write $H$ for its geometric strict henselization ring [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Let $b:R\to H$ be a ring homomorphism whose spectrum is the structural morphism [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. There exist a prime ideal $q\subset R$, a field $K$ which is a separable closure of the residue field of $A=R_q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], compatible residue-field and $A$-algebra structures on $K$, and an $A$-algebra structure on $H$ such that $A\to H$ composed with $R\to A$ equals $b$, and $H$ is an algebraic strict henselization of $A$ relative to $K$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization].

proof.text: Apply the affine neighbourhood/triples comparison to the identity chart of Spec R. The prime p is the image of the geometric point and K is the relative separable closure of its scheme residue field in Omega. Retain the universal affine-neighbourhood and triple cocones, their diagram equivalence, the structural R-map equation and the colimit-leg equation.

Compare the small representative colimit with the full affine-neighbourhood colimit by the canonical colimit isomorphism. Finality of the representative functor and uniqueness of universal cocones then identify the geometric strict henselization with the triple-cocone vertex. Each component of this ring isomorphism has its canonical coprojection formula.

The identity residue triple maps to every triple, so the triple cocone has one common structural R-map. Take a small representative of the identity pointed neighbourhood. The colimit-leg equations, the specified structural equation of the affine/triples equivalence, and naturality of the affine global-sections identification show that Spec of the transported R-map is strictLocalizationToBase. Faithfulness of Spec identifies this map with the prescribed b.

Apply the localized residue-triples strict-henselization theorem to the universal triple cocone, its comparison isomorphism and the common structural R-map. Set q to the underlying ideal of p. This gives the compatible separable closure, local-base algebra structure, structural-map equation and IsStrictHenselization conclusion. This is the retained upstream strictHenselizationRing_local_presentation proof.

theorem strictHenselizationRing_local_presentation
    (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (barY : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec R)
    (b : R ⟶ strictHenselization barY)
    (hb : Spec.map b = strictLocalizationToBase barY) :
    ∃ (q : Ideal R) (_ : q.IsPrime)
      (K : Type u) (_ : Field K)
      (_ : Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q)) K)
      (_ : IsSepClosure (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q)) K)
      (_ : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime q) K)
      (_ : IsScalarTower (Localization.AtPrime q)
        (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (Localization.AtPrime q)) K)
      (_ : Algebra (Localization.AtPrime q) (strictHenselization barY)),
      (∀ r : R, algebraMap (Localization.AtPrime q) (strictHenselization barY)
        (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime q) r) = b.hom r) ∧
      Algebra.IsStrictHenselization (Localization.AtPrime q) K
        (strictHenselization barY)
